_note: Board 1124:4562 is the OPTIMISE drill-in, and it is NOT the surface
`s3-flows-media-optimizing` already covers: that recipe measures board
303:2032, the media DRAWER while a copy is being written, whose subject is a
status pill on an asset card. This is the fourth view of AssetDetailOverlay —
preview well, Format chips, Quality slider, Original / Optimised rows, a
full-width CTA. Different board, different component, no overlap: the two
recipes share no node and no testId.
Like the image-editor board beside it, OptimizationPanel.tsx was already built
to 1124:4562 and cites it by number; what it lacked was an anchor, a probe
case and a recipe, so nothing had measured it.
REACHED VIA PROBE (`case=media-detail-optimize`) at the board's own 280x812:
the shipping AssetDetailOverlay with AutoOpen pressing the hub's Optimise row,
which is the door a person uses. The fixture asset is its own — the shared
1x1 GIF WebP-encodes TEN TIMES LARGER, so the panel drew its `+1069%` warning
branch, which is the one state 1124:4584 does not draw. A 2400x1600 SVG with a
padded comment gives a real starting byte count and a real saving.
WHAT MOVED:
1124:4584  the optimised figure is `--color/success-text` #057A55. It shipped
`--bk-success` #0E9F6E, which measures 3.39:1 on white at 11px —
a WCAG AA failure the board's own choice repairs. The warning
branch beside it (`--bk-warning` #C27803, 3.51:1) is the same
defect on a state no board draws, and moved with it to
`--bk-warning-text`; leaving it would have left one inaccessible
readout in a panel whose other one had just been fixed.
1124:4570  the format chips are 24 tall. `CHIP` said `tw:min-h-6`, which
cannot beat flowbite's `h-10` through twMerge (CLAUDE.md §Chrome),
so all three rendered 40. Same trap, same file-pair, as
ImageEditorModal's crop chips.
1124:4570  the active chip's fill is `--color/bg-selected` #EBF5FF. The class
named `--bk-accent-subtle` (#E1EFFE) with #EBF5FF as an
unreachable fallback — right colour, wrong token.
1124:4568  the preview line is `2400x1600 · 840 KB`: DIMENSIONS first, bytes
second. It printed the bytes alone, so the line that tells you
what you are about to shrink never said how big it is. The pixels
are read off the decoded image because this panel takes only a
`src` — the LibraryItem lives in the drill-in that hosts it.
NOT JOINED, and why:
1124:4567 the PREVIEW well and 1124:4585 the CTA — both fail on width by
exactly 2px, and the 2px is the drill-in's own 1px border. Figma strokes a
frame OUTSIDE and CSS draws it INSIDE, so a 280 board frame has a 278
content box; the board itself gives the preview `left-[-1px] w-[280px]`,
which is the designer compensating for that stroke, and puts the CTA at
left 15 with 17 to spare on the right for the same reason. The same artifact
is recorded on 297:2013 in `s1-1-coach-dismissed`. Their fills, heights and
radii all match and are in `measured/`.
1124:4570 / 4572 the chip BOXES and 1124:4566 / 4587 the back row and the
version note — hug-content widths taken from FIGMA's text metrics, not the
browser's: 'WebP' hugs to 57.6 in Chrome against the board's 52, and the
board's own two chips claim the same 52 for labels 10px apart in width. The
back row and the note are block/flex children in the DOM and text hugs in
Figma, which is not a comparison. All four LABELS are joined, which is where
the type contract lives, and the chip boxes' fills, heights and radii are
conformed in code.
1124:4574 the PNG chip — its export reads `w-[5px]` for a chip drawing the
word PNG. A bad export, not a design.
1124:4578 / 4579 / 4580 the quality slider's track, fill and thumb — `Slider`
is a shared chrome-ui primitive with its own boards; one screen board does
not re-settle it.
1124:4564 / 4565 the panel header's close control — `PanelFrame.Header` is
the shared 44h drawer header measured on the Media family's own boards
(144:2 and the drill-in frames). `panel-header` is anchored and SKIPPED so
the coverage ratchet can see it.
1682:7221 the prototype hotspot — Figma authoring furniture.
TEN UNKNOWNS, one cause: Figma exports auto line-height as `leading-[normal]`
and the code sets explicit leading (18 on the labels, 20 on the rows). A
keyword against a pixel value is not comparable, and deleting the leading to
make it comparable would be conforming to the instrument.
CONTRAST — ONE FAILURE, and it is the systemic pair, not this screen's doing:
4.39:1, the preview's mono size line, `--bk-ink-muted` on the well's
`--bk-bg-subtle`. See docs/design-jobs/FIGMA-TO-CODE/CONTRAST-INK-MUTED.md —
a token-value defect the boards themselves specify. The other two failures
this surface had are GONE, both fixed by conforming to the board.
Board sample data not conformed to: 'hero-dark.jpg', '840 KB', '312 KB · -63%'
and the quality 85 (which IS the shipped default, coincidentally).
